safetyNote: Listed as edible by DGfM and Swiss VAPKO, but DGfM marks Lactarius lignyotus Red List category 3 in Germany, and University of Lyon 1 recommends protecting it where declining. Follow local collection restrictions and avoid harvesting scarce populations. Do not identify an edible mushroom from its dark cap alone: inspect the pale gills, the short grooves at the top of the stem, the fresh white latex and the spruce association. Seek expert confirmation before food use and cook it adequately.

sections.title: Soot-dark velvet cap
sections.text: The cap is generally 3–8 cm across, sometimes a little larger, initially convex and later almost flat or slightly depressed, often retaining a distinct small central umbo. It is dry, strikingly velvety or finely felted and wrinkled, deep bistre to black-brown or nearly black, without concentric zones. The young margin is rolled inward and may show fine radial grooves; the fully grown edge may be wavy. Pale gills beneath make a strong visual contrast.

sections.title: White gills and pleated stem apex
sections.text: The moderately spaced white gills become cream with age, attach broadly to the stem and run down it only briefly; injuries may blush pink or reddish. The slender dark-brown to nearly black stem is velvety like the cap, with short longitudinal grooves or pleats directly beneath the gills, not a field of round pits. It is full when young and may hollow when mature. The pale flesh slowly turns pinkish to rusty at a cut.

sections.title: Milk and spruce habitat
sections.text: A fresh injury produces white latex, often in modest quantity. Sources disagree on whether isolated milk later yellows slightly, but agree that white milk touching injured flesh can leave a reddish or rusty mark. This fungus forms mycorrhizae mainly with spruce in upland and montane conifer woods, often on acidic soils, and fruits from summer to autumn. The similar dark L. picinus grows with spruce but lacks the same strong white-gill contrast and its milk becomes acrid; other dark milkcaps require careful comparison.

sections.title: Edibility and regional rarity
sections.text: DGfM and VAPKO list L. lignyotus among edible mushrooms. DGfM also records Red List category 3 in Germany; Lyon 1 advises protection because it is declining in its region. These conservation statements are regional, yet they make restrained collecting sensible wherever it is scarce. The illustration can show the pale gills and pleated stem apex, but cannot establish the host tree or delayed staining reactions.

traits: Dry deeply bistre to nearly black velvety cap, about 3–8 cm, often with small umbo and no zones
Moderately spaced white to cream gills, broadly attached and only shortly decurrent, reddening at injury
Slender dark velvety stem with short longitudinal grooves immediately beneath gills, not round pits
White latex; pale flesh slowly pinkish or rusty on injury
With spruce in upland or montane conifer woods, often on acidic soil, summer to autumn
Edible listing but German Red List category 3; regional conservation matters
